ProcessFaq.label: How we work
ProcessFaq.intro: The homepage should make our method clear: understand the operational problem, choose the right level of technology, and ship systems that users can actually adopt.

0.title: Clarify the real business constraint
0.description: We start from the operational bottleneck, not from a fashionable tool. The first question is always what needs to become faster, more accurate, more scalable, or easier to use.

1.title: Select the minimum viable architecture
1.description: Sometimes that means a lightweight Next.js app. Sometimes it means a computer-vision pipeline, background workers, containers, and inference services. We choose the smallest correct system.

2.title: Connect models, interfaces, and data flows
2.description: We treat the model, the API, the storage layer, and the product surface as one engineering problem, so the output is useful in the hands of real teams.

3.title: Iterate toward production readiness
3.description: After the first version works, we improve observability, reliability, deployment repeatability, and usability so the project can survive beyond the demo stage.

0.question: What kind of AI software can DevOP build?
0.answer: We build AI products and internal tools involving prediction, computer vision, speech processing, time-series analysis, and AI-assisted workflows. The common trait is that they are integrated into usable software, not isolated experiments.

1.question: Can you help if the project is still at MVP stage?
1.answer: Yes. Startup work is a strong fit for us because we can shape architecture, product scope, and implementation directly with founders or small teams, reducing the usual handoff overhead.

2.question: Do you only work on sports analytics?
2.answer: No. Sports analytics is one of our strongest proof areas because it combines real-time video, data engineering, and product design, but the same capabilities apply to enterprise workflows, operational dashboards, and domain-specific AI tools.

3.question: What stack do you usually use for scalable AI products?
3.answer: It depends on the problem, but our typical stack combines Next.js or React on the frontend, Python or Django for backend and AI workflows, PostgreSQL and Redis for data layers, and Docker-based deployment for reproducibility and scale.

about.p1: I embraced computer science for the sense of freedom it gives. The freedom to act, to create, to change and, when possible, to innovate.
about.p2: I graduated from Sapienza University of Rome, completing both my bachelor's and master's degrees with top marks. I am a dynamic person, sometimes contradictory, constantly evolving. I never stand still: my creative restlessness and the drive to challenge myself and push my limits are what keep me working for hours on a project I consider “mine.”
about.p3: After years of working while studying and gaining professional experience in different companies, I decided to give myself a different opportunity: to build something truly my own. I founded a startup, putting my experience, years of study and personal sacrifices at the service of my own ideas and vision. I design software architectures and develop full-stack solutions, integrating AI systems built to solve real-world problems.
about.p4: I am a positive, curious and meticulous person. I constantly question myself. I am always looking for new paths to explore, new ways to grow, and new projects worth dedicating myself to.

header.quote: "For the roads, they go on without end."

about.p1: Since the dawn of time, humanity has lived in God's shadow, seeking Him and envying His greatest privilege: the capacity to create. Condemned to finitude, man invented art to emulate that miracle, shaping stories and figures to feel like the master of a destiny.
about.p2: However, only computer science allows us to transcend the stasis of the canvas. Programming is the ultimate creative act, where logic becomes matter and thought becomes action. The thirst for omnipotence is quenched in every algorithm that works, in every system that springs to life beneath our fingers. If art imitates life, computer science simulates it. And in that microcosm of rules and variables, man finally touches the divine illusion of having created life itself.
about.p3: Perhaps one day the spell will break, for I have realized that giving life to one’s own creatures consumes the soul. Yet, it is a destiny I cannot evade. Every morning, facing the glow of the screen, I listen to that whisper which overpowers all reason: it is not a choice, it is a necessity. I must continue playing God until the voice of sleep screams louder than the voice of programming.

Targage.tagline: From surveillance footage to instant plate lookup
Targage.description: Targage is an intelligence layer for parking garages and private lots. It analyzes DVR/NVR footage, detects plates, extracts text, and creates a precise timeline so operators can retrieve entry and exit moments in seconds.
Targage.supporting: Instead of forcing operators to replace their camera stack, Targage acts as the brain layered on top of existing video systems: turning passive recordings into searchable evidence, operational history, and legal protection.

heroCard.brainDescription: Targage upgrades DVR and NVR footage with AI plate detection, OCR, and searchable timeline references without replacing the installed surveillance stack.
heroCard.securityDescription: Deployable as a secure software layer on local infrastructure or controlled environments, with clear data access boundaries and auditable retrieval.
heroCard.outcomeDescription: Hours of manual review become seconds of plate lookup, with clip references ready for operators, managers, and dispute handling.

efficiency.title: Operational efficiency
efficiency.desc: Targage is built for the real pain point: teams wasting hours reviewing recordings to answer simple vehicle-access questions. It compresses that effort into a fast search workflow.

legal.title: Legal protection
legal.desc: When surveillance exists, operators can be expected to reconstruct what happened. Targage helps turn footage into timestamped evidence instead of a liability trapped inside raw video archives.

integration.title: Logical upgrade
integration.desc: The product is not another closed hardware ecosystem. It is a software intelligence layer designed to sit on top of existing installations and add value without forcing an overhaul.

demo.title: Simulate how an operator retrieves a plate timeline
demo.description: This mock shows the user experience Targage aims for: search a plate, inspect the sightings timeline, and jump directly to the relevant clips instead of scrubbing through footage.
demo.complianceNote: Every result is designed to remain linked to original footage references, helping teams answer incidents with clear provenance and auditable access.
demo.emptyDescription: Try one of the suggested plates to see how Targage turns multiple sightings into a structured retrieval timeline.

ingestion.title: Video Ingestion
ingestion.desc: Processes live streams and historical recordings directly from existing DVR/NVR storage and surveillance feeds, preserving the installed hardware as the visual input layer.

detection.title: Detection + OCR
detection.desc: Locates license plates under real parking conditions such as glare, distance, and uneven lighting, then transcribes alphanumeric values through OCR and normalization logic.

indexing.title: Temporal Indexing
indexing.desc: Pairs each recognition event with timestamps, camera identity, and footage references in a structured searchable timeline that operators can query instantly.

retrieval.title: Instant Retrieval
retrieval.desc: Users search by plate number and retrieve the relevant entry, exit, and movement evidence immediately instead of manually reviewing long surveillance sessions.

time.title: Massive Time Savings
time.desc: Cuts video audit effort from hours of manual review to a few seconds per case.

security.title: Operational Security
security.desc: Creates a reliable chronological logbook of every vehicle movement inside the facility.

liability.title: Liability Protection
liability.desc: Provides timestamped visual evidence to resolve damage disputes quickly and transparently.

compatibility.title: Designed as a universal intelligence layer
compatibility.description: The strongest strategic angle for Targage is hardware disintermediation: keep the cameras, upgrade the logic. That makes the product easier to adopt for operators, integrators, and parking facilities already invested in surveillance infrastructure.

compliance.title: Privacy and sovereignty are product features
compliance.description: Targage should not be framed as reckless surveillance software. Its value increases when positioned as a controlled, auditable, privacy-aware layer that helps organizations handle video evidence more responsibly.

items.0: Deploy on local or controlled infrastructure when data sovereignty is a priority.
items.1: Support clear access rules, selective retrieval, and data-minimization-oriented workflows.
items.2: Help operators answer incidents with evidence faster, reducing unnecessary exposure to raw footage.

Targage.faqTitle: Questions operators and integrators actually ask
Targage.faqDescription: The page should answer practical concerns directly: compatibility, evidence retrieval, compliance, and the real operational advantage over manual review.

0.question: Does Targage require replacing the surveillance hardware?
0.answer: No. Its main value is acting as a software intelligence layer over existing camera systems, DVRs, and NVRs, reducing the need for expensive hardware replacement.

1.question: What problem does it solve better than manual CCTV review?
1.answer: It turns a time-heavy, error-prone review process into a plate-based search workflow, allowing staff to retrieve relevant entry and exit evidence in seconds instead of hours.

2.question: Why is legal and compliance positioning important here?
2.answer: Because parking operators often need to reconstruct events during disputes. A searchable timeline with footage references is more defensible and operationally useful than raw archives alone.

3.question: Who is Targage for?
3.answer: Parking operators, private garages, property managers, and system integrators who already have video infrastructure but need faster retrieval, better traceability, and a practical ANPR intelligence layer.
